title: [ORION-QG QG-37] One-corruption-resilient indexed probe identification
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Earned structural parents: QG-32 #911 (joint summaries + certified fixed separator), QG-32c #928 (exact universal noiseless fixed minimum 5), QG-34 #924 (exact noiseless adaptive minimax depth 3).
Fair noiseless fixed baseline: QG-35 #932 (pending exact accepted receipt at registration time).
Fair comparison: QG-36 #933 (frozen receipt composition, pending QG-35).

Donor areas to subtract: minimum test cover / distinguishing sensor placement; branch-and-bound test cover; active probing/adaptive diagnosis; separating systems and Ulam/Rényi liar games; noisy adaptive group testing; error-correcting codes.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE ROBUST-OBSERVATION FRONTIER. NO ROBUST CARDINALITY OR ADVANTAGE IS PREDICTED.**

All earned QG-32/QG-34 observation results assume exact probe answers. QG-37 asks a new robustness question:

> How many indexed structural probes are required so that the 715-way local-response identity remains uniquely recoverable after the joint bulk+spectrum summary is known, even if **one selected probe response is adversarially corrupted**?

This is an ORION-Q research-control robustness question, not a hardware-noise or quantum-measurement claim.

## Q1 — exact one-corruption fixed-code criterion

For a fixed selected probe set `P`, each orbit `o` has a multivalued response word `K_P(o)`.

Under at most one adversarially corrupted coordinate, unique decoding is possible iff every pair of distinct relevant orbit identities has Hamming distance at least 3:

`d_H(K_P(a), K_P(b)) >= 3`.

For one known joint summary class `S`, define `R1(S)` as the minimum cardinality of a fixed probe set selected after `S` is known such that every pair in `S` is distinguished on at least three selected probes.

Define `R1_* = max_S R1(S)`.

Also define `R1_universal` for one fixed probe set that works across all 92 joint classes. Keep the class-conditioned and universal quantities separate.

## Q2 — exact multicover formulation

For every orbit pair, probe `p` contributes one unit iff its exact responses differ. The robust fixed problem is therefore a minimum **3-cover of every pair**, not ordinary test cover.

Production exact method may use:
- pair-demand branch-and-bound with residual demand 0..3;
- safe dominance only when a probe's full pair-incidence dominates another's incidence;
- lower bounds from total residual demand / maximum marginal contribution and per-pair remaining candidates;
- QG-32/QG-35 noiseless solutions only as lower bounds or constructive seeds where logically valid, never as robust authority.

Generic ORION must use a different exact formulation, e.g. binary ILP / SAT / bounded exhaustive cardinality with constraints `sum_{p distinguishes pair} x_p >= 3`.

## Q3 — decoding certificate

For every positive robust result, serialize and verify:
- selected probe indices;
- minimum pairwise response-word Hamming distance;
- all pairs attaining the minimum distance;
- an exact nearest-codeword decoder or equivalent proof that every radius-1 corrupted word maps to at most one orbit within its known summary class.

A cardinality alone is insufficient.

## Q4 — robustness overhead

Only after QG-35 is exact may compare class-conditioned noiseless `F(S)` to robust `R1(S)`.

Define per-class overhead `R1(S)-F(S)` and worst overhead, but do not interpret this as physical noise cost. It is redundancy required for one-error authority robustness in the structural-probe interface.

## Q5 — ORION-Q consequence

A GREEN result may authorize a domain-specific fail-closed rule:
- when one structural probe answer may be unreliable, do not use a noiseless distinguishing set as identity authority;
- require an exact radius-1 robust probe code / decoder, or escalate to richer state/referee.

This extends the QG-derived authority router from query scope to **evidence reliability scope**.

## Independent verification

Production:
- exact response matrix reconstruction;
- exact minimum 3-cover per class and universal variant where tractable;
- explicit decoder/distance certificate.

Generic ORION:
- independent F2^2/F3 reconstruction;
- separate exact optimization formulation;
- independently recompute all pairwise distances and radius-1 decoding uniqueness.

Native ORION-Q:
- authorize only one-corruption structural-probe identity robustness on the frozen observation problem.

Workflow must require deterministic replay and reject a self-consistent tamper that lowers a claimed pairwise distance / removes a redundancy probe while recomputing result digest.

## Hard boundaries

Always false:
- hardware measurement noise model;
- stochastic physical error rate;
- fault-tolerant quantum-computing threshold claim;
- full finite-n optimum probes;
- generic coding/separating-system novelty;
- physical quantum advantage.

## Honest terminals

- `QG37_EXACT_ONE_CORRUPTION_FIXED_PROBE_CODE_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG37_ROBUST_FIXED_UPPER_BOUND_ONLY`
- `QG37_ROBUST_CODE_INFEASIBLE_IN_FROZEN_PROBE_LIBRARY`
- `QG37_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Donor subtraction

Minimum test cover, separating systems, error-correcting Hamming-distance criteria, adaptive diagnosis and noisy group testing are established donor ideas. Candidate value is only the exact TARE/QG-32 response-code geometry and its scoped ORION-Q evidence-reliability consequence.
